description: Lex Stella | Beni Mellal - Equipe Droit & Finance. Nous travaillons sur le droit spatial et l'économie de l'espace. Communication via groupe WhatsApp "Lex Stella".
summary:
Footprints in Forever is a virtual museum by team Lex Stella that gives a second life to forgotten NASA equipment left on the Moon and Mars.
The Problem: When missions end, rovers, landers and instruments are left behind and forgotten. Their stories disappear, even though they made space exploration possible.
Our Solution: We built an immersive digital museum where visitors can explore these forgotten objects. Our museum includes an interactive timeline that shows what was forgotten in each year and why it was forgotten. For each object, visitors can explore an interactive 3D model to see the whole machine from all sides, with all its general information, mission, date, location and story. Visitors can live the life of the machine and walk inside the museum from every angle.
We also created a Memories Wall, where every visitor can leave their own trace, share a message, and become part of the story. This transforms visitors from spectators into participants.
We used NASA open data and historical information to make the museum accurate, educational and emotional. Our goal is to make space history accessible, unforgettable, and alive for everyone, and to prove that nothing that touched the stars should ever be forgotten.
details:
Footprints in Forever is not a website. It is a living electronic museum for the machines and remnants humanity left behind on the Moon and Mars.

Your journey starts with a radio transmission calling you inside. You choose your world: Moon or Mars. Then you walk inside a full museum, through an interactive timeline, and face every forgotten machine and remnant.

Rotate it. Zoom into it. Click it. Discover who built it, why it was sent, where it went, and where it sleeps now. Live its life. Walk with it.

Travel with our Time Machine to any era and see the machines and remnants that lived then.

Then enter our 4 worlds:

1. Global Mission Control Center - 100 documented artifacts, 50 Moon + 50 Mars, 65 years of history from 1959 to today, from 6 nations.

2. NASA & International Data Archive - every artifact with real coordinates, real science, and real NASA sources. 100% verified.

3. The Memory Constellation - 100 stars. Left is Moon, right is Mars. Every dot is a soul. Click one, and its story wakes up.

4. The Memory Wall - the monolithic registry of extraterrestrial legacies, filterable by Rovers, Landers, Boosters and Sensors.

And finally, you don't just visit. You leave your mark.

In the Visitor Memory Registry, write your name, your city on Earth, dedicate your message to Opportunity, Luna 2, or Apollo 11, and become part of forever.

They are not debris. They are the first chapters of our story in space.
